redundancyOptions.label: One region, multiple zones
redundancyOptions.detail: Protects against selected zonal failures but not loss of the region.
redundancyOptions.normalConsequence: Normal traffic stays inside one region, keeping transfer and standby cost low.
redundancyOptions.failureConsequence: A regional loss removes the serving path until data, capacity, dependencies, and routing are restored elsewhere.

redundancyOptions.label: Warm recovery region
redundancyOptions.detail: A smaller standby receives replicated state and scales after promotion.
redundancyOptions.normalConsequence: The standby reduces regional recovery time without paying for two fully active stacks.
redundancyOptions.failureConsequence: The standby initially carries only 60% of target traffic, so load shedding or delayed work is required while capacity scales.

redundancyOptions.label: Two active regions with headroom
redundancyOptions.detail: Both regions serve traffic and each is sized to survive loss of its peer.
redundancyOptions.normalConsequence: Both paths are exercised continuously, but coordination, write ownership, and regional dependencies become more complex.
redundancyOptions.failureConsequence: The survivor has modeled headroom for full demand only if routing, data convergence, dependencies, and quotas work as tested.

managedDepthOptions.label: Infrastructure-led
managedDepthOptions.detail: Use general compute and portable engines; the team owns most lifecycle work.
managedDepthOptions.responsibility: The team owns host or cluster lifecycle, scaling, patching, backups, upgrades, and most recovery automation.
managedDepthOptions.exitAction: Rebuild provider infrastructure, identities, networks, and automation around a comparatively portable runtime and data engine.

managedDepthOptions.label: Selectively managed
managedDepthOptions.detail: Use managed compute and data services behind explicit application boundaries.
managedDepthOptions.responsibility: The provider owns more platform lifecycle; the team still owns configuration, access, data, application recovery, and service limits.
managedDepthOptions.exitAction: Replace managed APIs and identity bindings, export data, replay recovery tests, and revalidate performance in the new service.

managedDepthOptions.label: Deep managed-service integration
managedDepthOptions.detail: Adopt provider-specific event, data, identity, and operations capabilities.
managedDepthOptions.responsibility: Routine platform work falls, but the team must understand more provider contracts, quotas, degraded modes, and cross-service dependencies.
managedDepthOptions.exitAction: Redesign provider-specific workflows, translate data and policy, replace operational tooling, and run a staged migration with dual-write or replay controls.
